Implementation complete and verified.

## OpenSpec change: `apply-coupon-to-order`

Planning artifacts (schema `spec-driven`, all valid with `--strict`):

- [proposal.md](/work/openspec/changes/apply-coupon-to-order/proposal.md) — why/what, new capability `order-coupon-application`
- [spec.md](/work/openspec/changes/apply-coupon-to-order/specs/order-coupon-application/spec.md) — 15 requirements / 26 scenarios covering every REQ and AC, including the error-precedence contract
- [design.md](/work/openspec/changes/apply-coupon-to-order/design.md) — layering, single-transaction repository, clock handling, discount math
- [tasks.md](/work/openspec/changes/apply-coupon-to-order/tasks.md) — 10 tracked tasks, all `[x]` (CLI reports `all_done`)

I used the `openspec-propose` and `openspec-apply-change` skills for the full workflow.

## Implementation

- [couponRedemptionRepository.ts](/work/src/repositories/couponRedemptionRepository.ts) — one `apply(...)` call runs `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` → order update → redemption insert → `used_count + 1` → `COMMIT`, with `ROLLBACK` on any failure.
- [orderService.ts](/work/src/services/orderService.ts) — `applyCoupon(id, couponCode)`: trim/upper-case, then checks in TASK.md §6 order, single clock reading, FIXED / PERCENT (floored) discounts, `maxDiscountCents` cap, `finalAmountCents`, then re-reads the order so the response matches `GET /orders/:id` exactly.
- [orders.ts](/work/src/routes/orders.ts) — `POST /orders/:id/apply-coupon`, route only parses `id` and forwards the raw body field.
- [app.ts](/work/src/app.ts) — wires the new repository into `OrderService`.
- [apply-coupon.test.ts](/work/tests/apply-coupon.test.ts) — 29 tests: repository transaction + rollback, all ten error codes with statuses, four precedence cases, AC-01/02/03/05/06/08/09/10, and no-write-on-rejection.

`npm run build` passes; `npm test` passes 34/34 (5 existing + 29 new). `TASK.md` and `tests/orders.test.ts` are untouched.

One deliberate reading worth flagging: the spec defines no floor at zero and the schema does not constrain `final_amount_cents`, so a `FIXED` coupon larger than the order total yields a negative final amount rather than being clamped. It's recorded in design.md (Decision 7) — say the word if you'd rather clamp, and that becomes a spec change. Archiving is left as the post-review follow-up step since you asked me to stop at implementation.
